summary: Initial discovery for migrating inferencing from current mix of OpenAI hosted and self-hosted vLLM/TGI stacks. Aurum wants a predictable cost/latency path, strong security (VPC/KMS/SAML), and evaluation parity for their LLMs. Redwood AE+SE covered Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, suggested pilot approach, and agreed to run benchmarks and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood CSM), Raj Patel (CTO, Aurum), Sofia Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Daniel Kim (Infra), Priya Anand (Security), Ethan Lowe (SRE)

---
Summary (auto): Discussed migration path from OpenAI + vLLM self-host to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Focus on eval parity, security controls (KMS, SSO), throughput targets (500 rps burst, 50 rps steady), and pilot plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we can do intros quick, I'm Maya AE on the west coast.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Hi all, Raj here, CTO at Aurum, we've got a mix right now, some things on OpenAI for bursty customer-facing features and v L M self-host for heavier batch inference. Sorry my throat is rough.
[00:25] Sofia Ruiz: And Sofia, lead ML, we own model infra and evaluation. Our main thing is ensuring parity when we move, like we can't lose the reranker behavior and top-k stability.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Great, Liam SE from Redwood, I typically dig into perf and integration patterns. Quick question, what's your primary trigger for migrating—cost, latency, control, or something else?
[00:52] Daniel Kim: Hi, Daniel. From infra side it's all three. OpenAI costs spiked last quarter, and our v L M clusters are becoming harder to maintain—quantization issues and kernel differences. We want predictable unit economics.
[01:06] Priya Anand: Priya from security, we need VPC, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML and audit logs. Also data residency for EU customers, and SOC 2 evidence.
[01:20] Maya Chen: Thanks. That aligns with many customers. Briefly, Redwood offers Hosted API for fast get-started, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, and Private/VPC if you need customer-managed networking—each has tradeoffs.
[01:38] Raj Patel: Can you walk through compatibility? We use TGI locally and vLLM is our runtime. Our concern is checkpoints and tokenization differences.
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. Two parts: model artifacts and runtime behavior. We validate a lot of open models and have adapter layers for tokenizers and custom vocab. For vLLM/T G I there are sometimes KV-cache offsets and attention kernel differences that affect incremental decoding. We run parity evals—perplexity, reranking MRR, and long-context consistency.
[02:12] Sofia Ruiz: When you say parity evals, how automated is that? We have a 1200-prompt suite covering user queries, system messages, and high-recall re-ranker tests.
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: We can run that suite as part of a pilot. Typically we do a baseline on your current infra, then run the same prompts on Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated config. We capture latency P50/P95/P99, token cost, and quality metrics.
[02:40] Ethan Lowe: For production traffic, we see diurnal spikes up to 500 rps for small prompts and sustained 50 rps. Cold KV-cache costs blow up latency—do you have prefix or KV caching?
[02:53] Maya Chen: Yes, our runtime supports prefix/K V caching and automatic hot-prompt detection to keep latency low. For Dedicated we can tune cache retention and batching windows to meet your SLOs.
[03:06] Raj Patel: What about fallbacks? If a Dedicated pool goes down, can we route to Hosted or smaller models?
[03:13] Liam O'Connor: Smart routing is built-in. You can define policies by latency or cost; automatic fallback to compatible model variants is supported. We recommend canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies for model version changes.
[03:28] Priya Anand: From a compliance POV, we need key management—can Redwood integrate with our cloud KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key for private deploys?
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes, Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys in the Private/on-prem option. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[03:45] Sofia Ruiz: A deeper question on quantization—our self-host uses 4-bit QAT for cost reasons. Does Redwood support quantized execution and do you have recommendations?
[03:55] Liam O'Connor: We support a variety of quantization profiles; some kernels are quantization-friendly. We evaluate quality delta and throughput delta and recommend quantization only when quality regressions are within your guardrails. For many customers we recommend dynamic quant profiles per workload.
[04:12] Daniel Kim: Any known gotchas moving from TGI/vL M to your runtime? Tokenization differences, yes, but are there model-specific adjustments?
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: Sometimes special tokens or temperature seeds behave slightly different; we capture that during parity evals. We also look at KV cache warm-up patterns—if you're doing long-context dialogs, we might recommend sticky sessions to keep caches warm.
[04:38] Raj Patel: Pricing—do you have a ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated? We need a forecast for 12 months.
[04:46] Maya Chen: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet, but in general Hosted is pay-as-you-go, Dedicated is committed monthly which drives down unit cost with reserved GPU pools. We can model your 12-month forecast after we see the traffic profile.
[04:59] Ethan Lowe: On the pilot, we'd like to see a 2-week run with production-like traffic and a small canary in production. Can Redwood mirror traffic or replay traces?
[05:08] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can replay traces and also run a staged canary with your traffic using our routing policies. We recommend a canary that ramps to 10% then 50% before full cutover.
[05:22] Priya Anand: For audit logs—do you provide token-level logs or aggregated metrics? We can't store PII in logs.
[05:30] Maya Chen: We provide flexible logging; you can opt-in to token-level logs for debugging but for compliance we offer redaction, retention policies, and audit log exports to your SIEM.
[05:43] Raj Patel: Ok quick note, our EU customers require data residency. Is private deployment in aws eu-west-1 supported?
[05:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we have private plane options in EU regions via our Private offering or Dedicated in region. We'll include region options in the security pack.
[06:05] Sofia Ruiz: One nit, we've seen slight variance in beam search outputs between runtimes. How do you measure quality regressions?
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: We instrument evals for exact match, BLEU-like measures for structured outputs, and also business metrics—conversion lift or error rates. For reranking we use MRR and precision at K.
[06:27] [long pause / cross-talk]
[06:35] Daniel Kim: On infra complexity—if we choose Dedicated, who manages the OS/kernel updates and GPU drivers?
[06:42] Maya Chen: Redwood manages the serving runtime and GPU drivers for Dedicated. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you manage the host OS but Redwood provides the control plane and deployment tooling.
[06:55] Raj Patel: We need a plan for the first 90 days if we move forward. What does success look like?
[07:02] Maya Chen: Success criteria we typically propose: parity on your eval suite (quality), meeting latency SLOs (P95 under threshold), stable cost within forecast, and a safe rollback path. For the 90-day plan: pilot (2 weeks), tuning + canary (2–4 weeks), cutover plan (1–3 weeks).
[07:22] Sofia Ruiz: Can we get a checklist for what you need from us to run the pilot?
[07:27] Liam O'Connor: Yes, sample prompts/traffic, model checkpoints or model names, traffic traces, security contacts, and allowed IP ranges for VPC peering.
[07:38] Priya Anand: We will require an NDA before sending some of the data.
[07:42] Maya Chen: No problem, we'll route that to legal, but we'll start with a minimal dataset for benchmarking.
[07:50] Raj Patel: A couple technical clarifications—does Redwood have a recommended way to handle long-running sessions and context windows beyond 32k? We use a custom chunking layer.
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: We support large context models and recommend application-level chunking plus KV caching. For very long contexts we can offload embeddings to a vector store and use retrieval-augmented prompts.
[08:12] Ethan Lowe: On SLA, we need 99.9% uptime for some endpoints. Is that a Dedicated feature?
[08:19] Maya Chen: SLA-backed uptime is part of Dedicated and higher enterprise tiers. Hosted has standard uptime commitments but Dedicated can be contractually backed.
[08:30] Sofia Ruiz: Will Redwood help with retraining or is it strictly inference?
[08:34] Liam O'Connor: Primarily inference and model lifecycle for serving—versioning, rollouts, evals. For retraining we partner or can assist via referrals.
[08:45] Raj Patel: Any customers with similar stacks (OpenAI + v L M) you can point to?
[08:52] Maya Chen: We have a few references in fintech and healthcare who moved from mixed stacks—I'll share anonymized case studies.
[08:59] [10-minute block summarized — participants asking clarifying questions about batch windows and cost modeling]
[19:10] Liam O'Connor: On batching strategy—there's a latency/cost knob: increase batching window to improve throughput at expense of P50 latency. For user-facing low-latency endpoints we recommend 5–10ms batching windows and prefix caching.
[19:28] Sofia Ruiz: Are these knobs configurable per route?
[19:32] Liam O'Connor: Yes, per route and per model. You can set backlog size, max latency, and autoscale thresholds.
[19:42] Daniel Kim: For monitoring, do you expose token-level cost per request in the console?
[19:46] Nina Park: Nina from CSM—yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost, latency breakdown, per-route dashboards and tracing hooks.
[19:55] Raj Patel: We will need a walkthrough of the console, can we schedule that?
[19:59] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll schedule a demo next week.
[20:05] Priya Anand: Can you confirm retention windows for logs and how easy is it to purge data on demand?
[20:12] Maya Chen: We support configurable retention and on-demand purge APIs for Private and Dedicated; Hosted has default retention but enterprise plans can customize.
[20:25] Sofia Ruiz: On the subject of tokenization edge-cases, can we run a quick smoke test during pilot and flag any drift?
[20:32] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we'll run delta checks on tokenization and immediate output diffs and flag regressions.
[20:40] [30-second overlap, someone muted/unmuted]
[20:55] Raj Patel: Anything else? I'm worried about hidden costs—storage for KV caches, snapshotting models, etc.
[21:02] Maya Chen: Those are all measurable; we'll include KV cache storage estimates and snapshot storage in the pricing workbook.
[21:12] Daniel Kim: If we go Private on-prem, what's the lead-time and what hardware do you recommend?
[21:18] Liam O'Connor: On-prem timelines vary; usually 6–10 weeks including network setup. For hardware, we'll propose GPU SKUs based on model family—A100/RTX-class equivalents for float, and specialized inferencing cards for quantized workloads.
[21:32] Priya Anand: Do you do penetration testing or provide support for our third-party audits?
[21:37] Maya Chen: We can provide SOC2 reports, and we coordinate on penetration test scopes; for Private we can allow your auditors to validate deployments under NDA.
[21:49] [short pause]
[22:00] Nina Park: Quick recap and next steps: Maya will share security pack and pricing, Liam will run the benchmark once Sofia shares prompts, and we'll schedule a console demo.
[22:10] Sofia Ruiz: Yep I'll send the prompt corpus and traffic trace by Tuesday. We also want a check-in after the first benchmark run.
[22:18] Maya Chen: Great, we'll aim to get the security docs out by Wednesday and set up the benchmark timeline.
[22:26] Raj Patel: If we get parity and costs align, target is to migrate the first set of user-facing endpoints in the next 90 days.
[22:33] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[22:38] Ethan Lowe: One more: do you support function calling style or tool invocation patterns natively?
[22:44] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood supports structured output and function/tool calling patterns and we can help map your existing schema.
[22:52] Raj Patel: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[22:56] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next meeting.

---
Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcribed terms (v L M, vLMM), informal speech included. End of transcript.
notes: Customer is pragmatic and timeline-driven; security is a gating factor. Pilot is the critical path to get to firm pricing commit. Recommend rapid delivery on SOC2 docs and benchmarking to maintain momentum.
